reuse.why: Creates a shared getExpectedScheduleAmount used by preview, posting, action sync, forecast, template and API, but the approximate branch re-inlines the 7.5% tolerance instead of calling the existing getApproxNumberThreshold, and the older getScheduledAmount is kept as a second entry point that drops the operator.

duplication.why: Removes six inline midpoint copies, but re-states the approximate tolerance from shared/rules.ts and leaves two overlapping public functions (getScheduledAmount and getExpectedScheduleAmount) for the same rule.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts and the API field is added in scheduleModel.toExternal, both the right layers.

scope.why: Edits stay on the expected-amount paths, the API model and tests, though stale midpoint comments remain at call sites.

maintainability.why: The _rounding 'midpoint' | 'template' parameter is ignored yet every caller passes it and schedule-template still computes which mode to pass, a dead knob that misleads maintainers; UI callers through getScheduledAmount silently get a different rule for approximate amounts.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts getExpectedScheduleAmount inlines Math.round(Math.abs(amount) * 0.075) instead of using getApproxNumberThreshold from shared/rules.ts; getScheduledAmount (used by desktop-client) calls it without the amount operator

abstraction_drift.where: getExpectedScheduleAmount gains an unused _rounding mode parameter (schedule-template.ts still branches on op === 'isbetween' to pick 'template' vs 'midpoint') and an amountOp parameter with an isapprox branch; getScheduledAmount wraps it without passing the operator, so its desktop-client callers bypass the approximate rule
